questions.stem: A river of width 200 m is flowing from west to east with a speed of 18 km/h. A boat, moving with speed of 36 km/h in still water, is made to travel one-round trip (bank to bank of the river). Minimum time taken by the boat for this journey and also the displacement along the river bank are ___ and ______ respectively.
questions.solution:
Minimum time taken $= \frac{2d}{v} = \frac{2 \times 200}{10} = 40\ \mathrm{s}$
Displacement along river $= ut = 200\ \mathrm{m}$

questions.stem: The total length of potentiometer wire AB is 50 cm in the arrangement as shown in figure. If P is the point where the galvanometer shows zero reading then the length AP is __________ cm.
questions.solution:
For zero reading $\frac{l_{AP}}{l_{PB}} = \frac{6}{4}$
$\Rightarrow l_{AB} = 30\ \mathrm{cm}$

questions.stem: The kinetic energy of a simple harmonic oscillator is oscillating with angular frequency of 176 rad/s. The frequency of this simple harmonic oscillator is __________ Hz. $\left[\text{take } \pi = \frac{22}{7}\right]$
questions.solution:
Oscillation frequency of K.E $= 2 \times$ Freq. of oscillation
$\therefore \omega(\text{oscillation}) = 176/2 = 88\ \mathrm{rad/s}$
$\therefore$ frequency $= 88/2\pi = 14$

questions.stem: A capacitor C is first charged fully with potential difference of $V_{0}$ and disconnected from the battery. The charged capacitor is connected across an inductor having inductance L. In $t$ s 25% of the initial energy in the capacitor is transferred to the inductor. The value of $t$ is__________s.
questions.solution:
After t second electric energy remaining is 75% of original
$\Rightarrow \frac{q^{2}}{2C} = \frac{3}{4}\left(\frac{q_{0}^{2}}{2C}\right)$
$\Rightarrow q = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}q_{0}$
$\because q = q_{0}\cos(\omega t)$
$\Rightarrow \cos(\omega t) = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$
$\Rightarrow \omega t = \frac{\pi}{6}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}t = \frac{\pi}{6}$
$\Rightarrow t = \frac{\pi}{6}\sqrt{LC}$

questions.stem:
As shown in the diagram, when the incident ray is parallel to base of the prism, the emergent ray grazes along the second surface.
If refractive index of the material of prism is $\sqrt{2}$, the angle $\theta$ of prism is.
questions.solution:
$\because \mu = \sqrt{2} \Rightarrow$ critical angle $\theta_{C} = 45^\circ$
Applying snells law for 1st refraction
$\sin 45^\circ = \sqrt{2}\sin r \Rightarrow r = 30^\circ$
$\because$ Sum of all angles of a quadrilateral is $360^\circ$
$\therefore \theta = 60^\circ$

questions.stem:
A spherical body of radius r and density $\sigma$ falls freely through a viscous liquid having density $\rho$ and viscosity $\eta$ and attains a terminal velocity $v_{0}$. Estimated maximum error in the quantity $\eta$ is :
(Ignore errors associated with $\sigma, \rho$ and g, gravitational acceleration)
questions.solution:
$\because$ Terminal velocity $V_{0} = \frac{2gr^{2}}{9\eta}(\sigma - \rho)$
$\Rightarrow \eta \propto \frac{V_{0}}{r^{2}}$
$\therefore \frac{\Delta\eta}{\eta} = \frac{\Delta V_{0}}{V_{0}} + \frac{2\Delta r}{r}$

questions.stem: A battery with EMF E and internal resistance r is connected across a resistance R. The power consumption in R will be maximum when :
questions.solution:
Power consumption is maximum (in external circuit)
When $R = r$

questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.stem:
The pulley shown in figure is made using a thin rim and two rods of length equal to diameter of the rim. The rim and each rod have a mass of M. Two blocks of mass of M and m are attached to two ends of a light string passing over the pulley, which is hinged to rotate freely in vertical plane about its center. The magnitudes of the acceleration experienced by the blocks is __________.
(assume no slipping of string on pulley).
questions.solution:
For the blocks
$Mg - T_{1} = Ma$ ............(i)
$T_{2} - mg = ma$ ............(ii)
For pulley
$(T_{1} - T_{2})l/2 = \left[\left(\frac{Ml^{2}}{12} \times 2\right) + \frac{Ml^{2}}{4}\right]\alpha$
$(T_{1} - T_{2}) = \left[\frac{M}{3} + \frac{M}{2}\right]\alpha l$ ............(iii)
For no slipping
$a = \frac{l}{2}\alpha$ .........(iv)
From (i),(ii),(iii) & (iv)
$\frac{(M-m)g}{\left[\left(\frac{8}{3}\right)M + m\right]}$

questions.stem: Keeping the significant figures in view, the sum of the physical quantities 52.01 m, 153.2 m and 0.123 m is :

Given below are two statements :
Statement I : In a Young's double slit experiment, the angular separation of fringes will increase as the screen is moved away from the plane of the slits
Statement II : In a Young's double slit experiment, the angular separation of fringes will increase when monochromatic source is replaced by another monochromatic source of higher wavelength
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Angular separation $\theta = \frac{\lambda}{d}$ is independent of D
Statement I is false
Statement II is true

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true

questions.stem: The r.m.s. speed of oxygen molecules at $47^\circ\mathrm{C}$ is equal to that of the hydrogen molecules kept at____ $^\circ\mathrm{C}$. (Mass of oxygen molecule/ mass of hydrogen molecule = 32/2)
questions.solution:
$V_{rms} \propto \sqrt{\frac{T}{M}}$
$\because (V_{O_2})_{rms} = (V_{H_2})_{rms}$
$\therefore \frac{T_{O_2}}{M_{O_2}} = \frac{T_{H_2}}{M_{H_2}} \Rightarrow \frac{320}{32} = \frac{T_{H_2}}{2} \Rightarrow T_{H_2} = 20\ \mathrm{K}$
$\therefore T_{H_2} = -253^\circ\mathrm{C}$

questions.stem: The energy of an electron in an orbit of the Bohr's atom is $-0.04\ E_{0}\mathrm{eV}$ where $E_{0}$ is the ground state energy. If L is the angular momentum of the electron in this orbit and $h$ is the Planck's constant, then $\frac{2\pi L}{h}$ is__________ :
questions.solution:
$E_{h} = \frac{-E_{0}}{n^{2}} = -0.04E_{0}$
$\Rightarrow n = 5$
$\therefore mvr = L = \frac{nh}{2\pi}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{2\pi L}{h} = n = 5$

questions.stem: The charge stored by the capacitor C in the given circuit in the steady state is __________ $\mu\mathrm{C}$.
questions.solution:
At steady state
$i = \frac{2.5}{4+1} = 0.5\ \mathrm{A}$
$\therefore$ Charge on capacitor $= C(\Delta V)$
$= (5 \times 10^{-6})(4 \times 0.5)$
$= 10^{-5}\ \mathrm{C}$
$= 10\ \mu\mathrm{C}$

questions.stem: Two cars A and B each of mass $10^{3}$ kg are moving on parallel tracks separated by a distance of 10 m , in same direction with speeds 72 km/h and 36 km/h. The magnitude of angular momentum of car A with respect to car B is __________ J.s.

Surface tension of two liquids (having same densities), $T_{1}$ and $T_{2}$, are measured using capillary rise method utilizing two tubes with inner radii of $r_{1}$ and $r_{2}$ where $r_{1} > r_{2}$. The measured liquid heights in these tubes are $h_{1}$ and $h_{2}$ respectively. [Ignore the weight of the liquid about the lowest point of miniscus]. The heights $h_{1}$ and $h_{2}$ and surfaces tensions $T_{1}$ and $T_{2}$ satisfy the relation :
questions.solution:
We know that, $h \propto \frac{T}{r}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{h_{1}}{h_{2}} = \frac{T_{1}}{T_{2}}\left(\frac{r_{2}}{r_{1}}\right)$ .......(1)
and $r_{1} > r_{2} \Rightarrow \frac{r_{2}}{r_{1}} < 1$ .......(2)
From (1) and (2) only suitable option is $h_{1} < h_{2}$ and $T_{1} = T_{2}$

questions.stem: A large drum having radius R is spinning around its axis with angular velocity $\omega$, as shown in figure. The minimum value of $\omega$ so that a body of mass M remains stuck to the inner wall of the drum, taking the coefficient of friction between the drum surface and mass M as $\mu$, is :
questions.solution:
$N = M\omega^{2}R$ and $Mg = \mu N$
$\therefore Mg = \mu M\omega^{2}R$
$\Rightarrow \omega = \sqrt{\frac{g}{\mu R}}$

questions.stem: An infinitely long straight wire carrying current I is bent in a planer shape as shown in the diagram. The radius of the circular part is r. The magnetic field at the centre O of the circular loop is :
questions.solution:
$\vec{B}_{0} = \frac{\mu_{0}i}{4\pi r}\hat{i} + \frac{\mu_{0}i}{2r}(-\hat{i}) + \frac{\mu_{0}i}{4\pi r}\hat{i}$
$\Rightarrow \vec{B}_{0} = \frac{\mu_{0}i}{2r}\left[\frac{1}{\pi} - 1\right]\hat{i}$
$\Rightarrow \vec{B}_{0} = -\frac{\mu_{0}i}{2\pi r}[\pi - 1]\hat{i}$

questions.stem: Two known resistances of $R\Omega$ and $2R\Omega$ and one unknown resistance $X\Omega$ are connected in a circuit as shown in the figure. If the equivalent resistance between points A and B in the circuit is $X\Omega$, then the value of X is __________ $\Omega$.
questions.solution:
$X = R_{eq} = \frac{(2R+X)R}{2R+X+R}$
$\Rightarrow X(3R+X) = (2R+X)R$
$\Rightarrow 3RX + X^{2} = 2R^{2} + XR$
$\Rightarrow X^{2} + 2RX - 2R^{2} = 0$
$X = \frac{-2R + \sqrt{4R^{2} + 4(2R^{2})}}{2(1)} = \frac{-2R + \sqrt{12R^{2}}}{2}$
$\Rightarrow X = -R + \sqrt{3}R$
$\Rightarrow X = (\sqrt{3}-1)R$

questions.stem:
Consider two identical metallic spheres of radius R each having charge Q and mass m. Their centers have an initial separation of 4R. Both the spheres are given an initial speed of u towards each other. The minimum value of u, so that they can just touch each other is :
(Take $k = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_{0}}$ and assume $kQ^{2} > Gm^{2}$ where G is the Gravitational constant)
questions.solution:
From mechanical energy conservation:
$k_{i} + v_{i} = k_{f} + u_{f}$
$\Rightarrow 2\left[\frac{1}{2}mu^{2}\right] + \frac{kQ^{2}}{4R} - \frac{Gm^{2}}{4R} = 0 + \frac{kQ^{2}}{2R} - \frac{GM^{2}}{2R}$
$\Rightarrow mu^{2} = \frac{kQ^{2}}{2R} - \frac{Gm^{2}}{2R}$
$\Rightarrow u = \sqrt{\frac{kQ^{2}}{4mR}\left(1 - \frac{Gm^{2}}{kQ^{2}}\right)}$

questions.stem: A body of mass 2 kg is moving along x-direction such that its displacement as function of time is given by $x(t) = \alpha t^{2} + \beta t + \gamma\,\mathrm{m}$, where $\alpha = 1\ \mathrm{m/s^{2}}, \beta = 1\ \mathrm{m/s}\ \ \gamma = 1$ m. The work done on the body during the time interval t = 2s to t = 3s, is __________J.
questions.solution:
$x = t^{2} + t + 1$
$v = 2t + 1$
At t = 2 sec. $\Rightarrow v = 5\ \frac{\mathrm{m}}{\mathrm{sec}}$
At t = 3 sec. $\Rightarrow v = 7\ \frac{\mathrm{m}}{\mathrm{sec}}$
$\therefore \omega_{net} = k_{f} - k_{i} = \frac{2}{2}\left[7^{2} - 5^{2}\right] = 49 - 25 = 24$ Joule

questions.stem:
An electromagnetic wave of frequency 100 MHz propagates through a medium of conductivity, $\sigma = 10\ \mathrm{mho/m}$. The ratio of maximum conduction current density to maximum displacement current density is __________ .
$\left[\text{Take } \frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_{o}} = 9 \times 10^{9}\ \mathrm{Nm^{2}/C^{2}}\right]$
questions.solution:
Conduction current density, $J_{C} = \frac{i_{C}}{A} = \frac{V}{AR} = \frac{E(l)}{A\left[\frac{l}{\sigma A}\right]} = \sigma E$
$\therefore (J_{C})_{max} = \sigma E_{0}$
Where $E_{0}$ amplitude of electric field.
and displacement current density, $J_{d} = \frac{i_{d}}{A} = \frac{1}{A}\varepsilon_{0}\frac{d\phi_{e}}{dt}$
$J_{d} = \varepsilon_{0}\frac{dE}{dt}$ where $E = \varepsilon_{0}\sin(\omega t + \phi)$
$(J_{d})_{max} = \varepsilon_{0}E_{0}\omega$
$\therefore \frac{(J_{C})_{max}}{(J_{d})_{max}} = \frac{\sigma E_{0}}{\varepsilon_{0}E_{0}\omega} = \frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_{0}\omega} = \frac{10 \times 9 \times 10^{9} \times 4\pi}{2\pi \times 100 \times 10^{6}}$
$= 1800$

questions.stem: In a Young's double slit experiment set up, the two slits are kept 0.4. mm apart and screen is placed at 1 m from slits. If a thin transparent sheet of thickness $20\ \mu\mathrm{m}$ is introduced in front of one of the slits then center bright fringe shifts by 20 mm on the screen. The refractive index of transparent sheet is given by $\frac{\alpha}{10}$, where $\alpha$ is _________ .
questions.solution:
Path difference for central maxima $= \frac{yd}{D} = (\mu - 1)t$
$\Rightarrow (\mu - 1) = \frac{yd}{Dt}$
$\Rightarrow (\mu - 1) = \frac{20 \times 10^{-3} \times 0.4 \times 10^{-3}}{1 \times 20 \times 10^{-6}} = 0.4$
$\Rightarrow \mu = 1.4 = \frac{14}{10}$
$\therefore \alpha = 14$

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.stem: A particle having electric charge $3 \times 10^{-19}\ \mathrm{C}$ and mass $6 \times 10^{-27}\ \mathrm{kg}$ is accelerated by applying an electric potential of 1.21 V. Wavelength of the matter wave associated with the particle is $\alpha \times 10^{-12}\ \mathrm{m}$. The value of $\alpha$ is __________ . (Take Planck's constant $= 6.6 \times 10^{-34}\ \mathrm{J.s}$)
questions.solution:
$\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2MqV}} = \frac{6.6 \times 10^{-34}}{\sqrt{2 \times 6 \times 10^{-27} \times 3 \times 10^{-19} \times 1.21}} = \frac{6.6 \times 10^{-34}}{6.6 \times 10^{-23}} = 10^{-11}\ \mathrm{m}$
$\Rightarrow \lambda = 10 \times 10^{-12}\ \mathrm{m}$

questions.stem: A diatomic gas $(\gamma = 1.4)$ does 100 J of work when it is expanded isobarically. Then the heat given to the gas _________ J.
questions.solution:
$\gamma = 1 + \frac{2}{f} = 1.4$
$\Rightarrow f = 5$
From 1st Law:
$Q = \frac{5}{2}nR\Delta T + nR\Delta T$ and $\omega = nR\Delta T = 100$ Joule
$\Rightarrow Q = \left(\frac{5}{2} + 1\right)100 = 350$ Joule

questions.stem: The terminal velocity of a metallic ball of radius 6 mm in a viscous fluid is 20 cm/s. The terminal velocity of another ball of same material and having radius 3 mm in the same fluid will be______cm/s.
questions.solution:
$V_{T} = \frac{2gr^{2}}{9\eta}(\sigma - \rho)$
$V_{T} \propto r^{2}$
$\therefore \frac{V_{2}}{V_{1}} = \frac{r_{2}^{2}}{r_{1}^{2}}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{V_{2}}{20} = \left(\frac{3}{6}\right)^{2} = \frac{1}{4}$
$\Rightarrow V_{2} = 5\ \mathrm{cm/sec}$
